answer: Place agents into randomly assigned bonded audit pools. A pool handling basalt samples, onyx inventories, or beacon readings must have members independently co-sign a result after receiving hidden test cases. If an audit later finds fabrication, every signer loses a proportional bond and the pool's future quota falls. One operator cannot cheaply fill a pool with aliases because colluding keys share liability and need separate locked capital. Expanding a Sybil farm therefore requires many funded identities that accept correlated slashing risk. This assumes audits can identify false results.
